card.name: Route word right before infusion
card.fires_on: The last piece of the route word (intravenous, subcutaneous, IV) or a bracket right after a rate, when the word "infusion" is expected next. It is seen in dosing text about bolus followed by continuous infusion.

modes.label: Route word before infusion
modes.description: The ending of intravenous or subcutaneous, or the abbreviation IV, directly before the word infusion.
modes.example: followed immediately by a 1.75 mg/kg/h intr<<avenous>> infusion for the duration of the procedure.

modes.label: After an infusion rate
modes.description: A bracket or IV right after a per-minute rate, leading into infusion dose.
modes.example: 36 to 300 mcg/kg (bolus dose) or 4.8 to 13.7 mcg/kg/min<< (>>infusion dose).

card.writes: It suppresses muscle and intramuscular tokens, so it steers the next word away from intramuscular routes and toward infusion.
card.plain: It lights up when a drug's route is named just before the word infusion, as in bolus then continuous IV infusion.
